title: Manipur: from accession to merger
body: A few days before Independence, the Maharaja of Manipur, Bodhachandra Singh, signed the Instrument of Accession with the Government of India. He did so on the assurance that the internal autonomy of Manipur would be maintained. Under the pressure of public opinion, the Maharaja held elections in Manipur in June 1948, and the state became a constitutional monarchy. In the new Legislative Assembly there were sharp differences over whether Manipur should merge with India: the state Congress wanted the merger, while other political parties opposed it. In September 1949 the Government of India succeeded in persuading the Maharaja to sign a Merger Agreement, completing its full merger with the Indian Union.
